title: Annotatio V §.II Ratiocinative: Unanimous in fundamentals — one spiritual body more than not, though lesser dissent remains
pass_a_gloss: Ratiocinative: Because those unanimous in the Fundamental and so necessary and chief dogmas of the Christian Religion, though dissenting in others less fundamental and less necessary, yet striving meantime toward a greater and perfect Unity, in Charity, are more one and the same Spiritual Body than they are not; or (what comes to the same) are more contained in the Consociation of one and the same Christian Church than they are not — seeing that denomination is from the greater part.
pass_b_english: By reason: those agreed on the fundamental — and so necessary and chief — dogmas of the Christian religion, though they still differ on lesser points, yet press on toward fuller unity in charity.
They are more one spiritual body than not.
Or, what comes to the same, they are more held in the Consociation of one Christian church than they are shut out of it — for we name a thing from its greater part.
source_text: Ratiocinative: Quia in Fundamentalibus eoque necessariis praecipuisque Christianae Religionis dogmatibus unanimes, licèt in aliis minus fundamentalibus minusque necessariis dissentientes, ad majorem intereà perfectamque Unitatem contendentes, in Charitate, unum idemque Spirituale Corpus magis sunt, quàm non sunt; vel (quod eodem recurrit) unius ejusdemque Ecclesiae Christianae Consociatione continentur magis, quàm non continentur: Quandoquidem à potiori fit denominatio.
